newsitem.title: USA: PSA lauds Congress de minimis pact, eyes Clinton.
newsitem.headline: PSA lauds Congress de minimis pact, eyes Clinton.

text.p: Bond dealers are delighted that U.S. House and Senate tax negotiators agreed to back off a House plan to slash the two percent de minimis exemption for corporate municipal bond holdings, a spokesman said Friday.
But it is far too early to declare victory, added Micah Green, executive director of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, in a telephone interview.
Green said the White House, a strong supporter of de minimis repeal, could still push for reinstatement of the proposal during negotiations with Capitol Hill over the tax package.
"This is an extremely positive development," Green said. "It means we can go the next step."
He added, "But the situation is still very fluid. This congressional agreement is but a negotiating document for the White House and Congress."
Therefore, PSA and issuers nationwide will not let up their aggressive campaign to lobby Congress, and now the White House, on their views, Green said.
Reuters reported Thursday that House and Senate conferees tentatively agreed to drop the House's proposal to cut back the de minimis exemption for corporate holdings of munis to a flat $1 million.
And on Friday, the Bureau of National Affairs published the text of the proposed Republican conference agreement that makes it official that the House dropped its plan.
Currently, the Internal Revenue Service does not permit businesses to deduct interest on debt that they use to finance the purchase of tax-exempt bonds.

But IRS said that in 1972 -- in what has been dubbed the de minimis rule -- that it will not monitor whether a corporation has borrowed to purchase tax-exempt bonds as long as those holdings total less than two percent of net assets.
The Clinton Administration this winter called for repeal of the two percent de minimis rule, dubbing it corporate welfare.
